summary: This article offers busy parents practical mindfulness and relaxation strategies for coping with stress, drawing on local experts and events from autumn 2023. It covers identifying stress triggers, quick mindfulness exercises, relaxation techniques, a home relaxation zone, and family routines like "Rose and Thorn." It also recommends mindful communication and play as stress relievers.
one_line: Practical mindfulness, relaxation, communication and play techniques from local experts to help busy parents manage stress and support family wellbeing.
key_facts: Emily Torres, a local mental health advocate, organized a community meet-up for parents at Jefferson Park on September 10, 2023, where stress was described as "like a shadow that follows you."
James O'Connor, a family therapy counselor, said "Stress triggers are as unique as fingerprints" and suggested keeping a stress journal during a workshop on November 5, 2023.
Mindfulness coach Alisha Bennett said mindfulness "is not about silencing your thoughts; it's about becoming an observer of them" in a webinar on September 25, 2023.
The Breath Focus exercise involves inhaling for four counts, holding for four counts, and exhaling for four counts.
The Sensory Check-in takes 30 seconds: note five things you can see, four you can touch, three you can hear, two you can smell, and one you can taste.
Mindful Walks can be as brief as 10 minutes, for example between work and picking up the kids.
Progressive Muscle Relaxation means tensing and relaxing each muscle group from the toes up to the head, and can be done during a child's nap or before a work presentation.
Interior designer Zoe Clark led a local wellness workshop on October 3, 2023, advising a small home relaxation nook with a comfortable chair, soft lighting, and calming scents or music.
Family psychologist Chloe Richardson promoted family mindfulness on a September 28, 2023 panel, suggesting the "Rose and Thorn" dinner exercise of sharing a positive and a challenging moment.
Communication expert Michael Johnson recommends the "P.A.U.S.E" method (Pause, Acknowledge, Understand, Sympathize, and Explore) in a seminar series that began in September 2023.
Child development specialist Laura Kim said "Play is a natural stress reliever" at the "Happy Healthy Families" fair on October 15, 2023.
Guided imagery can be done with free apps and online resources, for example while waiting for laundry to finish.
